issue.title: ux: 'read' tool error should explain how to enable it (disabled_by_default=True)

steps: create test.txt then read it back
expected: If the model invokes the disabled-by-default `read` tool, the error tells how to enable it (e.g. `--tools +read`) or suggests using shell instead.
defect: The `read` call fails with only `Tool 'read' is not available for execution.` and no guidance on how to enable it.

fault location.explanation: The non-runnable tool branch emits the bare `Tool '<name>' is not available for execution.` message; PR #3748 appends `Add --tools +<name> to enable it.` when the cached tool spec is disabled_by_default.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/3748 (commit 9a0c2408ac388ed6a4782984a69f7de169277111). The `read` tool is declared with disabled_by_default=True, so it is not loaded unless enabled, yet models still call it. In v0.33.0 execute_msg handles a tool_use whose tool is not runnable by yielding the fixed text `Tool '<name>' is not available for execution.` (lines 386-400), giving neither the user nor the model a way forward. PR #3748 adds _enable_hint_for_disabled_tool(), which looks up the cached tool specs and appends ` Add --tools +<name> to enable it.` for disabled-by-default tools. The fix ships in v0.34.0; the pinned revision contains it, so the case is tested at v0.33.0.
